Reproducing LeMessurier et al. (2019) from CRCNS ssc-10¶

Paper. LeMessurier AM, Laboy-Juarez KJ, McLain K, Chen S, Nguyen T, Feldman DE (2019). Enrichment drives emergence of functional columns and improves sensory coding in the whisker map in L2/3 of mouse S1. eLife 8:e46321. doi:10.7554/eLife.46321. The claims file was written from the version of record (PMC6697414), with its Methods, Table 1 and figure supplement legends.

Data set. CRCNS ssc-10, "2-photon calcium imaging in S1 of enriched and normally housed mice during individual deflection of 9 whiskers" (LeMessurier & Feldman 2019, doi:10.6080/K0DB801M), read from the public bucket at https://crcnsarchive.s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/ssc-10/live/. CRCNS data sets have no versions, so the version is recorded as unversioned; this is the only copy the archive holds (data descriptor version 0.6, Aug 15 2019; data.tar.gz last modified 2026-02-11 on the bucket). The paper cites the data set by its DOI without a version. The file read is data.tar.gz, MD5 80bcef52304d27c9e039e7027fe09ff4 in the data set's checksums.md5; the notebook computes the MD5 of the stream it reads and compares it (data check). The data set's sample_code.zip (MD5 c3cd644bb9072bd4b63c96de5496a119) was read for method details and is cited where used; it is not run.

What the data set holds. For each of 36 imaging fields (folders <mouse>/<date>/[f#]), three MATLAB files: raw and neuropil fluorescence per movie (processed_data.mat), dF/F, stimulus tables, trial-aligned traces, stored responsiveness p-values and ROI positions relative to the nine barrel centres (reduced_data.mat), and acquisition settings (settings.mat). The juxtacellular recordings of Figure 1F and the barrel areas of Figure 2 S2 are not in it.

How it is read. The 4.7 GB tar file is streamed once, without writing to disk, and each field is reduced to per-trial evoked responses as it arrives (helper ssc10.py). In the last three runs this took 7 to 10 minutes (431 to 582 s), and the whole notebook 14 to 24 minutes.

The folders hold 22 Drd3-Cre (L2/3) and 14 Scnn1a-Cre (L4) fields, every movie at 29.92 Hz (Methods: 30 Hz), with an evoked window of 30 frames after 15 baseline frames, as the descriptor and the Methods say. The stimulus code of Stimuli.Label (k is the whisker whisk[k] of settings.mat, 9 a blank trial) agrees with the per-whisker frame lists in every field; the descriptor does not state it. Field DNH13b/20161208/f2 has no trials for E1, E2 and E3: those whiskers are missing from its traceByStim, which the descriptor does not mention. Three fields have one dF/F movie without a Stimuli entry. processed_data.mat holds more ROIs than reduced_data.mat in 21 of 36 fields (1044 against 998 in NH L2/3, 1276 against 1147 in EN L2/3); the paper says ROIs with nuclear GCaMP were excluded, which may account for part of this. The sponTrace blank trials are fewer than the trials Label marks blank (for example 51 of 61 in the first field), with no stated rule. In three L4 fields (ScENR10c/20180104/f1, ScENR10c/20180110, ScENR10b/20180105/f2) sponTrace holds 76-frame segments that start 0.5 s after each blank onset, where every other field stores 106 frames starting 0.5 s before onset, as traceByStim does (next cell); in those fields the blank trials are cut from the stored dF/F at every Label 9 onset.

# dF/F: the stored traces against a rebuild from processed_data.mat (first movie of each field).
dchk = pd.DataFrame([dict(field=f["field"], layer=f["layer"], npSub=f["npSub"],
                          rebuild_own_r=f["dff_rebuild_maxdiff"], subtract_then_filter=f["dff_subtract_first_maxdiff"],
                          methods_4frame_p20=f["dff_methods_maxdiff"])
                     for f in F])
print("Largest absolute difference from the stored dF/F, per field (dF/F units). rebuild_own_r: 5-frame median of the")
print("ROI and neuropil traces, then subtraction at the field's own weight (0 for L2/3, 0.3 for L4), F0 the 5th percentile;")
print("subtract_then_filter: the same with the subtraction before the filter; methods_4frame_p20: 4-frame median, 20th percentile, r = 0.")
print(dchk.groupby(["layer", "npSub"])[["rebuild_own_r", "subtract_then_filter", "methods_4frame_p20"]].describe().round(4).T.to_string())
# Evoked responses rebuilt at r = 0 (L2/3) and r = 0.3 (L4) against those of the stored traces.
rows = []
for f in F:
    rw = 0.0 if f["layer"] == "L23" else 0.3
    a = np.concatenate([f["np"][rw]["ev"][w].ravel() for w in ssc10.WHISKERS
                        if f["np"][rw]["ev"][w].shape == f["ev"][w].shape])
    b = np.concatenate([f["ev"][w].ravel() for w in ssc10.WHISKERS if f["np"][rw]["ev"][w].shape == f["ev"][w].shape])
    ok = np.isfinite(a) & np.isfinite(b)
    rows.append(dict(field=f["field"], layer=f["layer"], r=rw, corr=np.corrcoef(a[ok], b[ok])[0, 1],
                     max_abs_diff=np.abs(a[ok] - b[ok]).max(), blank_match_maxdiff=f["np_blank_match_maxdiff"],
                     blank_stored=f["np_blank_n"][0], blank_rebuilt=f["np_blank_n"][1], nonfinite_rois=f["np_nonfinite_rois"]))
evchk = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("\nPer-trial evoked responses rebuilt from raw fluorescence against the stored traces:")
print(evchk.groupby("layer")[["corr", "max_abs_diff", "blank_match_maxdiff"]].describe().round(4).T.to_string())
print("Blank trials, stored (sponTrace) and rebuilt (Label 9), summed over fields:", evchk.groupby("layer")[["blank_stored", "blank_rebuilt"]].sum().to_dict("index"))
print("ROIs with non-finite stored or rebuilt traces, left out of the blank match:", evchk.groupby("layer").nonfinite_rois.sum().to_dict())
print("Blank trials are matched one to one (each rebuilt trial used at most once), at the field's own weight.")
odd = [(f["field"], f["spon_len"], f["trace_len"]) for f in F if f["spon_len"] != f["trace_len"]]
print("Fields whose sponTrace segments differ in length from traceByStim (field, sponTrace, traceByStim frames):", odd)

The stored dF/F of every field is reproduced from processed_data.mat to within 0.019 dF/F by a 5-frame moving median and F0 the 5th percentile of each movie, with, for L4 (npSub = 1), 0.3 of the neuropil trace subtracted after filtering and before dF/F, as the data descriptor says ("after temporal filtering and before deltaF/F calculation"). Subtracting before filtering leaves L4 differences of 0.21 to 0.60. With the Methods' 4-frame median and 20th percentile the largest difference per field is 0.17 to 3.5: the data follow the pipeline code (deltaF_simple.m, as the claims file reports it), not the Methods. Per-trial evoked responses rebuilt this way match the stored ones (correlation 1.000, largest difference below 0.01), and every stored blank trial is matched one to one by a rebuilt Label 9 trial to within 0.013 (89 L2/3 ROIs with non-finite traces left out of the match).

# Stimulus timing: population mean dF/F around whisker and blank onsets, every field.
lags = F[0]["onset_lags"] / F[0]["fs"]
resp_win = (lags >= 0) & (lags < 1)
pre_win = (lags >= -0.5) & (lags < 0)
rows = []
for f in F:
    s, b = f["onset_trace_stim"], f["onset_trace_blank"]
    d = s - b
    # contrast in the 1 s after onset against the same contrast with the onsets shifted by -2 s and +2.5 s
    shift = {sh: (np.roll(d, -int(round(sh * f["fs"])))[resp_win] - np.roll(d, -int(round(sh * f["fs"])))[pre_win].mean()).mean()
             for sh in (-2.0, 0.0, 2.5)}
    rows.append(dict(field=f["field"], layer=f["layer"], stim_minus_blank_0_1s=shift[0.0],
                     shifted_m2s=shift[-2.0], shifted_p2_5s=shift[2.5], peak_lag_s=lags[np.argmax(d)]))
clock = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(clock.round(4).to_string(index=False))
print("\nFields where the whisker-minus-blank contrast in 0-1 s exceeds both shifted contrasts:",
      int(((clock.stim_minus_blank_0_1s > clock.shifted_m2s) & (clock.stim_minus_blank_0_1s > clock.shifted_p2_5s)).sum()), "of", len(clock))
fig, ax = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10, 3))
for f in F:
    ax[0 if f["layer"] == "L23" else 1].plot(lags, f["onset_trace_stim"] - f["onset_trace_blank"], lw=0.7)
for a, t in zip(ax, ("L2/3", "L4")):
    a.axvline(0, color="k", lw=0.5); a.set_title(f"{t}: whisker minus blank, population mean dF/F"); a.set_xlabel("s from onset")
plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()
print("Fields whose difference peaks 0.3 to 1.4 s after onset:", int(clock.peak_lag_s.between(0.3, 1.4).sum()), "of", len(clock))
print("Fields where the shifted contrasts are not exceeded:", clock[~((clock.stim_minus_blank_0_1s > clock.shifted_m2s) & (clock.stim_minus_blank_0_1s > clock.shifted_p2_5s))].field.tolist())
print("Range of plotted values:", round(min((f["onset_trace_stim"] - f["onset_trace_blank"]).min() for f in F), 3),
      "to", round(max((f["onset_trace_stim"] - f["onset_trace_blank"]).max() for f in F), 3))

Stimulus timing: in 30 of 36 fields the population mean dF/F after whisker onsets exceeds that after blank onsets more in the 1 s after onset than with the onsets shifted by -2 s or +2.5 s, and the peak of the difference lies 0.3 to 1.4 s after onset in 28 fields. This is consistent with the stimulus table and the dF/F sharing one clock. In the six other fields (printed above), where the whisker-minus-blank difference of the mean over all ROIs is small, the shared clock was not established by this test.

In [6]:
# Barrel radius per field and barrel: ROI_pos_barrel / ROI_pos_barrel_norm (one scalar per barrel?).
rows = []
for f in F:
    ratio = np.linalg.norm(f["pos"], axis=-1) / np.linalg.norm(f["posn"], axis=-1)   # R x 9
    for j, w in enumerate(ssc10.WHISKERS):
        r = ratio[:, j]
        r = r[np.isfinite(r)]
        if len(r) == 0:
            continue
        rows.append(dict(field=f["field"], mouse=f["mouse"], layer=f["layer"], group=f["group"], barrel=w,
                         radius=np.median(r), spread=(r.max() - r.min()) / np.median(r)))
radii = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print("Relative spread (max - min) / median of the ratio over a field's ROIs, per barrel: median",
      round(radii.spread.median(), 4), ", max", round(radii.spread.max(), 4))
print("Radius (um) by layer and group, over fields and barrels:")
print(radii.groupby(["layer", "group"]).radius.describe().round(1).to_string())
# ROI positions: distance to the nearest barrel centre, inside against outside ROIsInBarrel
d_in, d_out = [], []
for f in F:
    dist = np.linalg.norm(f["pos"], axis=-1)
    distn = np.linalg.norm(f["posn"], axis=-1)
    inb = f["barrel"] != ""
    j = np.array([ssc10.WHISKERS.index(b) if b else -1 for b in f["barrel"]])
    d_in += list(distn[inb, j[inb]])
    d_out += list(distn[~inb].min(1))
print("Normalised distance to the ROI's own barrel centre, ROIs listed in ROIsInBarrel: max", round(max(d_in), 3),
      "; ROIs listed in no barrel: min distance to any centre", round(min(d_out), 3))

ROI_pos_barrel_norm is not ROI_pos_barrel divided by one radius per barrel: the ratio varies by a median 37% over the ROIs of a field, so the normalisation uses a radius along each ROI's direction, and no barrel radius or area is stored. ROIs listed in ROIsInBarrel lie within 1.27 normalised radii of their barrel's centre and unlisted ROIs at least 0.85 from any centre, which is consistent with the barrel boundaries being drawn from histology outlines, not circles.

Mice, fields and cells¶

table1-mice-and-fields¶

The population imaging used 7 NH and 7 EN Drd3-Cre mice with 11 imaging fields each, and 5 NH and 6 EN Scnn1a-Tg3-Cre mice with 6 and 8 imaging fields.

Folder names carry the genotype (D for Drd3-Cre, Sc for Scnn1a-Tg3-Cre) and the housing (NH, ENR); the data descriptor's <mouse ID>\<experiment date>\<imaging field number> layout gives the fields.

Responsiveness¶

The Methods' test (claims file, opening comment) is run on every ROI: a one-sided permutation test of the difference in mean evoked dF/F between whisker and blank trials, 10,000 shuffles, Benjamini-Hochberg over the nine whiskers at 0.05. The variant is the data set's stored permTestResults, corrected the same way and without ROIs whose traces contain NaN, as the data set's sample code (find_sigROIs.m) does.

In [8]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(101)
t0 = time.time()
ssc10.responsiveness(F, rng)
print(f"responsiveness tests: {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")
rows = []
for f in F:
    inb = f["barrel"] != ""
    crow = np.isin(f["barrel"], ["c1", "c2", "c3"])
    rows.append(dict(layer=f["layer"], group=f["group"], total=f["n_rois"], total_raw=f["n_rois_raw"], total_C123=crow.sum(),
                     resp_methods=f["resp_methods"].sum(), resp_methods_barrel=(f["resp_methods"] & inb).sum(),
                     resp_methods_C123=(f["resp_methods"] & crow).sum(),
                     resp_stored=f["resp_stored"].sum(), resp_stored_barrel=(f["resp_stored"] & inb).sum(),
                     resp_stored_C123=(f["resp_stored"] & crow).sum()))
cc = pd.DataFrame(rows).groupby(["layer", "group"]).sum()
cc["frac_resp_methods"] = (cc.resp_methods / cc.total).round(3)
print(cc.to_string())
agree = np.concatenate([f["resp_methods"] == f["resp_stored"] for f in F])
print(f"\nROIs on which the Methods' test and the stored p-values agree: {agree.mean():.3f}")
print("Stored p-values: smallest value", min(np.nanmin(f["p_stored"]) for f in F),
      "; Methods' test smallest possible 1/10001 =", round(1 / 10001, 6))

fig1f-gcamp-matches-spikes¶

Whisker receptive fields measured from GCaMP6s dF/F were highly similar to those from simultaneously recorded spikes in 9 of 10 L2/3 neurons.

The data set holds no cell-attached recordings: every field above is a Drd3-Cre or Scnn1a-Cre population imaging field, and the data descriptor lists only the three MATLAB files per field. This claim is blocked.

Per-ROI measures¶

For each responsive ROI: the evoked response per whisker as the median over trials (the receptive field of the Methods) and as the mean; the median z-scored to the blank trials, centred on the blank mean (z, the claims file's reading) and on the blank median (zmed, the variant; it is what the data set's sample code plotPointRep_CRCNS.m computes); the best whisker (BW, largest mean; best_med by the median); equivalent best whiskers under readings E1, E2 (10,000 shuffles) and E3 (medians, 1,000 shuffles); the distance in um to each of the nine barrel centres. L2/3 uses all responsive ROIs of a field (reading A) unless a cell says otherwise; L4 uses responsive ROIs in barrels C1 to C3 (Methods), all responsive L4 ROIs as the variant.

Point representation (Figure 2)¶

Each responsive ROI enters once per reference whisker, at its distance to that whisker's barrel centre, with its z-scored median response to that whisker (claims file, opening comment). Bins are 75 um (Figure 2A legend; binEdges=0:75:1050 in the data set's sample code). EN against NH per bin by the two-sided permutation test of the difference in means (10,000 shuffles).

In [12]:
BINS = np.arange(0, 1051, 75)


def pointrep(tb, ar, layer, zkey="z", sel=None, rng=None, bins=BINS):
    m = (tb.layer == layer).values
    if sel is not None:
        m = m & sel
    out = []
    for b0, b1 in zip(bins[:-1], bins[1:]):
        r = {}
        for g in ("NH", "EN"):
            mm = m & (tb.group == g).values
            d, z = ar["dist"][mm], ar[zkey][mm]
            inb = (d >= b0) & (d < b1) & np.isfinite(z)
            r[g] = z[inb]
            r[g + "_mice"] = np.repeat(tb.mouse.values[mm][:, None], 9, 1)[inb]
        diff, p = ssc10.perm_test_means(r["EN"], r["NH"], rng)
        out.append(dict(bin=f"{b0}-{b1}", n_NH=len(r["NH"]), NH=r["NH"].mean(), sem_NH=ssc10.sem(r["NH"]),
                        n_EN=len(r["EN"]), EN=r["EN"].mean(), sem_EN=ssc10.sem(r["EN"]), diff=diff, p=p))
    return pd.DataFrame(out).set_index("bin")


L23_READINGS = {}
rng = np.random.default_rng(301)
for resp, tb, ar in (("methods", T, A), ("stored", TS, AS)):
    for roi_reading, sel in (("A", None), ("B", tb.inb.values)):
        for zkey in ("z", "zmed"):
            L23_READINGS[(resp, roi_reading, zkey)] = pointrep(tb, ar, "L23", zkey, None if sel is None else sel, rng)
main = L23_READINGS[("methods", "A", "z")]
print("L2/3, Methods responsiveness, reading A, z centred on the blank mean:")
print(main.round(4).to_string())

In L2/3, EN raised the mean response to a reference whisker in and just around its column, at 0-75 um (NH 0.59, EN 0.77), 150-225 um (0.53, 0.60) and 225-300 um (0.41, 0.51) from the column centre.

rows = []
for key, pr in L23_READINGS.items():
    rec = dict(responsive=key[0], rois=key[1], zscore=key[2])
    tests, within = [], []
    for b, (nh, tnh, en, ten) in EXP.items():
        rec[f"NH {b}"] = round(pr.loc[b, "NH"], 3); rec[f"EN {b}"] = round(pr.loc[b, "EN"], 3); rec[f"p {b}"] = pr.loc[b, "p"]
        tests.append(pr.loc[b, "diff"] > 0 and pr.loc[b, "p"] < 0.05)
        within += [abs(pr.loc[b, "NH"] - nh) <= tnh, abs(pr.loc[b, "EN"] - en) <= ten]
    rec["tests_hold"] = int(sum(tests)); rec["values_within"] = int(sum(within))

fig2b-2d-point-representation¶

Two-dimensional maps of the L2/3 point representation, with fields rotated to align the arc axis, show the same EN enhancement in the home column and reduction some distance away.

The claim is judged on the EN minus NH mean response over ROI-whisker entries inside the average barrel radius of the reference column, and beyond 375 um (to 750 um), as the criterion says. The mean radius is the mean over L2/3 fields and barrels of the radius from ROI_pos_barrel_norm (data check). The 2D map is drawn with axes along the row and arc of each field, from the barrel centres (ROI_pos_barrel relative to two barrels gives the vector between their centres).

def field_axes(f):
    """Unit vectors along the row (arc number increasing) and the arc (C to E) in a field's image frame."""
    c = {}
    for j, w in enumerate(ssc10.WHISKERS):
        ok = np.isfinite(f["pos"][:, j, 0]) & np.isfinite(f["pos"][:, 0, 0])
        c[w] = np.nanmean(f["pos"][ok, 0, :] - f["pos"][ok, j, :], 0)   # centre of barrel w relative to C1
    row = np.nanmean([c[r + "2"] - c[r + "1"] for r in "cde"] + [c[r + "3"] - c[r + "2"] for r in "cde"], 0)
    arc = np.nanmean([c["d" + a] - c["c" + a] for a in "123"] + [c["e" + a] - c["d" + a] for a in "123"], 0)
    return row / np.linalg.norm(row), arc / np.linalg.norm(arc), c

fig2c-l4-sharper-than-l23¶

In [19]:
def sharp(pr):
    nh = pr["NH"]
    ratio = nh["225-300"] / nh["0-75"]
    below = [b for b in nh.index if nh[b] < 0.5 * nh["0-75"]]
    return ratio, below[0] if below else None

        rows.append(dict(responsive=resp, l23_rois=rr, l4_rois=sel, zscore=zkey, ratio_L23=round(r23, 3), ratio_L4=round(r4, 3),
                         half_L23=h23, half_L4=h4,

figs2-1-column-frame¶

In a column-based reference frame, EN raised the mean L2/3 response to a reference whisker in its home column, sharpened the point representation mainly across rows, and reduced its spatial bias toward adjacent higher-arc columns; in L4 EN weakened home-column responses.

Positions in units of the reference barrel's radius along the ROI's direction (ROI_pos_barrel_norm), ROIs within 5 radii; home column below 1. Directions are taken from each field's row and arc axes (the vectors between barrel centres). Across rows means within 45 degrees of the arc axis; across arcs, within 45 degrees of the row axis.

In [20]:
def frame_entries(tb, ar, layer, sel=None, zkey="z"):
    m = (tb.layer == layer).values
    if sel is not None:
        m = m & sel
    rows = []
    for i in np.where(m)[0]:
        f = F[tb.fi.iat[i]]
        rowv, arcv, _ = AXES[f["field"]]
        for j in range(9):
            p = f["pos"][tb.row.iat[i], j]
            dn = ar["distn"][i, j]
            if not np.isfinite(dn) or dn > 5:
                continue
            x, y = p @ rowv, p @ arcv
            ang = np.degrees(np.arctan2(y, x))   # 0 = toward higher arc, 90 = toward the next row
            rows.append((tb.group.iat[i], dn, ang, ar[zkey][i, j]))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows, columns=["group", "dn", "ang", "z"])


rng = np.random.default_rng(401)
res = []
for resp, tb, ar in (("methods", T, A), ("stored", TS, AS)):
    for zkey in ("z", "zmed"):
        e23 = frame_entries(tb, ar, "L23", None, zkey)
        e4 = frame_entries(tb, ar, "L4", tb.c123.values, zkey)
        rec = dict(responsive=resp, zscore=zkey)
        for lay, e in (("L23", e23), ("L4", e4)):
            h = e[e.dn < 1]
            d, p = ssc10.perm_test_means(h[h.group == "EN"].z, h[h.group == "NH"].z, rng)
            rec[f"{lay} home NH"] = round(h[h.group == "NH"].z.mean(), 3); rec[f"{lay} home EN"] = round(h[h.group == "EN"].z.mean(), 3)
            rec[f"{lay} home p"] = p
        ring = e23[(e23.dn >= 1) & (e23.dn < 2)]
        a = ring.ang.abs()
        across_rows = ring[(a > 45) & (a < 135)]
        across_arcs = ring[(a <= 45) | (a >= 135)]
        plus_arc = ring[a <= 45]
        minus_arc = ring[a >= 135]
        g = lambda df, grp: df[df.group == grp].z.mean()
        rec["rows EN-NH"] = round(g(across_rows, "EN") - g(across_rows, "NH"), 3)
        rec["arcs EN-NH"] = round(g(across_arcs, "EN") - g(across_arcs, "NH"), 3)
        rec["bias NH (+arc - -arc)"] = round(g(plus_arc, "NH") - g(minus_arc, "NH"), 3)
        rec["bias EN (+arc - -arc)"] = round(g(plus_arc, "EN") - g(minus_arc, "EN"), 3)
        rec["n ring rows/arcs"] = (len(across_rows), len(across_arcs))
        res.append(rec)
print(pd.DataFrame(res).to_string(index=False))

Result: not reproduced. The L2/3 home-column response is higher in EN under every reading, significantly with the stored p-values (0.602 against 0.697, p = 0.0058; blank-median z p = 0.0083; Methods' test p = 0.19 and 0.069). The L4 home-column response is not lower in EN at p < 0.05 under any reading (p = 0.40 to 1.0). The two readings of the shape hold in all four readings: at 1-2 radii EN minus NH is -0.051 across rows and +0.050 across arcs, and the +1 minus -1 arc bias is +0.236 in NH and -0.135 in EN (Methods' test, blank-mean z). The criterion's partial outcome needs both home-column tests.

figs2-2-barrel-size-unchanged¶

Enrichment did not change the radius of L4 barrels, in Drd3-Cre mice (NH 151 um, EN 145 um) or in Scnn1a-Cre mice (NH 118 um, EN 124 um).

The data set holds no barrel areas. The radius used is the median over a field's ROIs of ROI_pos_barrel / ROI_pos_barrel_norm for each barrel, which is the barrel's radius along the ROIs' directions (a stated approximation, as the criterion allows), averaged over a mouse's fields. Each mouse's mean is over its nine barrels; the ANOVA is on the per-barrel radii per mouse.

Result: partially reproduced. The two-way ANOVA finds no enrichment effect in either genotype (Drd3-Cre p = 0.20, Scnn1a-Cre p = 0.27). The mouse means are Drd3-Cre NH 148.2 and EN 155.8 um, Scnn1a-Cre NH 119.1 and EN 126.5 um; three are within tolerance, Drd3-Cre EN is 10.8 um above 145 (tolerance 4.6), and stays 153.5 to 157.1 um when any one mouse is left out. The data set has 7 Drd3-Cre NH mice; leaving any one out gives 144.4 to 153.6 um. The radii are taken from the normalised ROI positions, along the ROIs' directions, not from barrel areas, which the data set does not hold, so the one miss cannot be told apart from the error of this approximation.

Tuning (Figure 3)¶

An entry is a responsive ROI and a reference whisker; its distance is to that whisker's barrel centre. Tuned by BW means the BW is the reference whisker; by eBW, the reference whisker is among the eBWs.

In [22]:
def tuning_entries(tb, ar, layer, sel=None):
    m = (tb.layer == layer).values
    if sel is not None:
        m = m & sel
    idx = np.where(m)[0]
    bw = np.array([ssc10.WHISKERS.index(b) for b in tb.best.values[idx]])
    bwm = np.array([ssc10.WHISKERS.index(b) for b in tb.best_med.values[idx]])
    out = []
    for j in range(9):
        out.append(pd.DataFrame(dict(group=tb.group.values[idx], mouse=tb.mouse.values[idx], ref=j,
                                     dist=ar["dist"][idx, j], bw=bw == j, bw_med=bwm == j,
                                     e1=ar["e1"][idx, j], e2=ar["e2"][idx, j], e3=ar["e3"][idx, j],
                                     has=np.isfinite(ar["z"][idx, j]))))
    e = pd.concat(out)
    return e[e.has & np.isfinite(e.dist)]


def bin_of(d, bins=BINS):
    k = np.digitize(d, bins) - 1
    return np.array([f"{bins[i]}-{bins[i + 1]}" if 0 <= i < len(bins) - 1 else "far" for i in k])


ENT = {}
for resp, tb, ar in (("methods", T, A), ("stored", TS, AS)):
    for rr, sel in (("A", None), ("B", tb.inb.values)):
        e = tuning_entries(tb, ar, "L23", sel)
        e["bin"] = bin_of(e.dist.values)
        ENT[("L23", resp, rr)] = e
    for rr, sel in (("C1-C3", tb.c123.values), ("all L4", None)):
        e = tuning_entries(tb, ar, "L4", sel)
        e["bin"] = bin_of(e.dist.values)
        ENT[("L4", resp, rr)] = e
print("Entries per layer, responsiveness and ROI reading:", {k: len(v) for k, v in ENT.items()})

E3 (medians) is computed only for the Methods' responsiveness.

Result: partially reproduced. By BW the NH fractions are within tolerance: 54.2%, 14.9% and 1.7% (Methods' test, reading A, BW by mean; paper 53, 16, 1), and 50.9%, 16.7% and 1.5% with the stored p-values and the BW by median, where the bin counts are also within tolerance (57 and 406; the Methods' test gives 48 in the 0-75 um bin). By eBW no reading of the claims file comes near: 89.6% to 96.5% at 0-75 um, 56.9% to 67.7% at 225-300 um and 34.8% to 44.8% at 525-600 um (paper 67, 43, 10). Fractions fall with distance under every reading. In the exploratory cell, outside the criterion, E1 gives 4.05 eBWs per NH ROI on average, and a one-sided test lowers the 0-75 um fraction only to 87.5%; requiring each eBW to be itself a responsive whisker gives 72.9% (one-sided) or 75.0% (E1), 41.0% or 43.7% at 225-300 um and 15.6% or 16.3% at 525-600 um, near the paper's values. That reading is not in the paper, and decides no outcome.

discussion-l23-nh-in-column-tuning¶

In NH L2/3, about 48% of cells located in a column responded maximally to the CW and 65% had the CW among their equivalent best whiskers.

    idx = np.where(m)[0]
    cw = np.array([ssc10.WHISKERS.index(b) for b in tb.barrel.values[idx]])
    d = pd.DataFrame(dict(col=tb.barrel.values[idx], bw=tb.best.values[idx] == tb.barrel.values[idx],
                          bw_med=tb.best_med.values[idx] == tb.barrel.values[idx],
                          e1=ar["e1"][idx, cw], e2=ar["e2"][idx, cw], e3=ar["e3"][idx, cw]))
    for bwk in ("bw", "bw_med"):
        for ek in ("e1", "e2", "e3"):
            if ek == "e3" and resp == "stored":
                continue
            pooled_b, pooled_e = 100 * d[bwk].mean(), 100 * d[ek].mean()
            percol = d.groupby("col")[[bwk, ek]].mean() * 100
            rows.append(dict(responsive=resp, bw=bwk, ebw=ek, n=len(d), BW_pooled=round(pooled_b, 1), eBW_pooled=round(pooled_e, 1),
                             BW_per_column=round(percol[bwk].mean(), 1), eBW_per_column=round(percol[ek].mean(), 1),
                             columns=len(percol)))
disc = pd.DataFrame(rows)
disc["pooled within"] = (abs(disc.BW_pooled - 48) <= 4.8) & (abs(disc.eBW_pooled - 65) <= 6.5)
disc["per-column within"] = (abs(disc.BW_per_column - 48) <= 4.8) & (abs(disc.eBW_per_column - 65) <= 6.5)
print(disc.to_string(index=False))

Result: partially reproduced. Pooled over the 375 NH L2/3 ROIs over a barrel, 48.8% have the CW as BW (paper 48; 45.6% to 49.6% over the BW and responsiveness readings), but 84.9% to 88.1% have the CW among the eBWs (paper 65). The mean over columns of the per-column fraction gives 34.4% to 37.3% and 82.3% to 86.4%, neither within tolerance. The exploratory eBW reading that requires responsiveness gives 71.5% to 73.9% within columns (exploratory cell under figs3-1-l23-salt-and-pepper).

figs3-1-l4-nh-tuning¶

In NH L4, 63% (30/48) of cells within 75 um of a column centre had the CW as BW and 73% (35/48) had it among eBWs, not different from L2/3; but the fraction tuned to a whisker fell off more sharply with distance in L4, significantly at 150-375 um.

Result: not reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after round 3 of the verification). In NH L4 (C1-C3, Methods' test, E1) 64.3% of the 56 entries within 75 um have the CW as BW and 75.0% among the eBWs (paper 63% and 73%, both within tolerance), and the BW fraction does not differ from L2/3 (54.2%, Fisher p = 0.32). By eBW, L4 is lower than L2/3 in all three bins from 150 to 375 um under every reading (Methods' test, C1-C3, E1: p = 2e-8, 6e-11, 3e-12; every reading p < 1e-5); by BW in one or two. But the eBW fraction at 0-75 um is lower in L4 than in L2/3 (75.0% against 91.7%, p = 0.036; E2 p = 0.0051; 0.026 and 0.0055 with the stored p-values), against the claimed absence. Under E3 that test is not significant (p = 0.40), but the L4 value is 82.1%, outside 73 +/- 7.3. The criterion's partial clause needs both 0-75 um values within tolerance and both absence tests not significant, and no reading meets it, as for figs2-1-column-frame and fig4ae-l4-weaker-responses. Every other part of the claim holds. The eBW absence fails because the NH L2/3 eBW fraction (89.6-96.5%) is far above the paper's 67%, which traces to the unresolved eBW definition, so the failure may lie in this attempt and not in the paper.

fig3a-l23-enrichment-more-cw-tuned¶

In L2/3, EN raised the fraction of cells tuned to the CW at column centres (82%, 111/135, against 67% in NH) and in every bin below 300 um, not beyond; over all cells within column boundaries 77.1% (468/607) against 65.1% (224/344).

def within_columns(tb, ar, layer, sel, ek):
    out = {}
    for g in ("NH", "EN"):
        m = (tb.layer == layer).values & (tb.group == g).values & tb.inb.values
        if sel is not None:
            m = m & sel
        idx = np.where(m)[0]
        cw = np.array([ssc10.WHISKERS.index(b) for b in tb.barrel.values[idx]])
        out[g] = ar[ek][idx, cw]
    k = [int(out[g].sum()) for g in ("NH", "EN")]
    n = [len(out[g]) for g in ("NH", "EN")]
    p = stats.fisher_exact([[k[1], n[1] - k[1]], [k[0], n[0] - k[0]]])[1]
    return k, n, p

Result: not reproduced. At 0-75 um the EN fraction tuned to the CW is lower than NH under every reading (for example 82.7% against 91.7%, Fisher p = 0.16, Methods' test, E1), and over ROIs within columns the fractions are equal (84.8% of 640 against 85.3% of 375, p = 0.86). EN is not significantly higher in any bin below 300 um; it is significantly lower from 375 to 675 um (p = 0.0019 to 0.010). The EN values (82.7%, 84.8%) are near the paper's (82%, 77.1%); the NH values (91.7%, 85.3%) are far above its 67% and 65.1%. Under the exploratory eBW reading that requires responsiveness, NH falls to 75.0% and 73.9%, but EN is still not higher (77.4%, p = 0.84; within columns 75.9%, p = 0.50).

Receptive fields (Figure 4)¶

Responses are the z-scored medians (z; zmed as the variant). EN against NH by the two-sided permutation test of the difference in means, ROIs as units.

In [29]:
def ranked(tb, ar, layer, sel=None, zkey="z"):
    m = (tb.layer == layer).values
    if sel is not None:
        m = m & sel
    out = {}
    for g in ("NH", "EN"):
        z = ar[zkey][m & (tb.group == g).values]
        z = z[np.isfinite(z).all(1)]           # ROIs with all nine whiskers (DNH13b lacks the E row)
        out[g] = -np.sort(-z, axis=1)
    return out


def rank_tests(rk, rng):
    rows = []
    for k in range(9):
        d, p = ssc10.perm_test_means(rk["EN"][:, k], rk["NH"][:, k], rng)
        rows.append(dict(rank=k + 1, NH=rk["NH"][:, k].mean(), EN=rk["EN"][:, k].mean(), diff=d, p=p))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("rank")


RANKED = {}
rng = np.random.default_rng(501)
for resp, tb, ar in (("methods", T, A), ("stored", TS, AS)):
    for rr, sel in (("A", None), ("B", tb.inb.values)):
        for zkey in ("z", "zmed"):
            RANKED[(resp, rr, zkey)] = rank_tests(ranked(tb, ar, "L23", sel, zkey), rng)
print("n ROIs with all nine whiskers (Methods, A):", {g: len(v) for g, v in ranked(T, A, "L23").items()})

fig4b-l23-cw-and-best-sw-stronger¶

In L2/3, EN increased the signal-to-noise of the CW response and of the two best surround whisker responses.

In [31]:
def cw_sw(tb, ar, layer, sel=None, zkey="z"):
    m = (tb.layer == layer).values & tb.inb.values
    if sel is not None:
        m = m & sel
    out = {}
    for g in ("NH", "EN"):
        idx = np.where(m & (tb.group == g).values)[0]
        cw = np.array([ssc10.WHISKERS.index(b) for b in tb.barrel.values[idx]])
        z = ar[zkey][idx]
        cwz = z[np.arange(len(idx)), cw]
        sw = z.copy(); sw[np.arange(len(idx)), cw] = np.nan
        sw = -np.sort(-np.where(np.isfinite(sw), sw, -np.inf), axis=1)[:, :8]
        sw[~np.isfinite(sw)] = np.nan
        out[g] = (cwz, sw)
    return out


rng = np.random.default_rng(502)
rows = []
for resp, tb, ar in (("methods", T, A), ("stored", TS, AS)):
    for zkey in ("z", "zmed"):
        o = cw_sw(tb, ar, "L23", None, zkey)
        rec = dict(responsive=resp, zscore=zkey, n=(len(o["NH"][0]), len(o["EN"][0])))
        d, p = ssc10.perm_test_means(o["EN"][0], o["NH"][0], rng)
        rec["CW NH/EN"] = f"{o['NH'][0].mean():.3f}/{o['EN'][0].mean():.3f}"; rec["CW p"] = p
        ok = [d > 0 and p < 0.05]
        for k in range(3):
            d, p = ssc10.perm_test_means(o["EN"][1][:, k], o["NH"][1][:, k], rng)
            rec[f"SW{k + 1} NH/EN"] = f"{np.nanmean(o['NH'][1][:, k]):.3f}/{np.nanmean(o['EN'][1][:, k]):.3f}"; rec[f"SW{k + 1} p"] = p
            if k < 2:
                ok.append(d > 0 and p < 0.05)
        rec["CW, SW1, SW2 EN higher p<0.05"] = int(sum(ok))
        rows.append(rec)
print(pd.DataFrame(rows).to_string(index=False))

fig4c-spontaneous-activity¶

EN decreased spontaneous (blank trial) activity in L2/3, while L4 spontaneous activity was unaffected.

Spontaneous activity: the median over blank trials of the evoked-window response (baseline subtracted); the variant is the median evoked-window dF/F without baseline subtraction (spont_level, from the stored deltaF at the blank onsets of Stimuli).

The Figure 4C legend's "median ΔF/F during blank trials" reads as the variant; this is asked as a question on the claims file. Over all L4 ROIs, not only C1-C3, EN is lower by the variant (p = 0.0003).

figs4-1-absolute-dff¶

Without normalisation to spontaneous activity, L2/3 cells in EN had greater mean evoked dF/F than NH, and the regression of weakest-four on strongest-four whisker responses had a different slope in EN, showing sharper tuning.

Per ROI the mean evoked dF/F per whisker (mean over trials), sorted; the four strongest and four weakest are averaged. Slopes are compared by the interaction term of an OLS fit.

In [33]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(504)
rows = []
for resp, tb, ar in (("methods", T, A), ("stored", TS, AS)):
    m = (tb.layer == "L23").values
    d = []
    for g in ("NH", "EN"):
        mm = ar["mean"][m & (tb.group == g).values]
        mm = mm[np.isfinite(mm).all(1)]
        s = -np.sort(-mm, axis=1)
        d.append(pd.DataFrame(dict(group=g, strong=s[:, :4].mean(1), weak=s[:, 5:].mean(1), all9=mm.mean(1))))
    d = pd.concat(d)
    rec = dict(responsive=resp, n=(int((d.group == "NH").sum()), int((d.group == "EN").sum())))
    for k in ("strong", "all9"):
        diff, p = ssc10.perm_test_means(d[d.group == "EN"][k], d[d.group == "NH"][k], rng)
        rec[f"{k} NH/EN"] = f"{d[d.group == 'NH'][k].mean():.4f}/{d[d.group == 'EN'][k].mean():.4f}"; rec[f"{k} p"] = p
    fit = smf.ols("weak ~ strong * C(group, Treatment('NH'))", data=d).fit()
    term = [t for t in fit.params.index if t.startswith("strong:")][0]
    for g in ("NH", "EN"):
        rec[f"slope {g}"] = round(smf.ols("weak ~ strong", data=d[d.group == g]).fit().params["strong"], 4)
    rec["slope diff (EN-NH)"] = round(fit.params[term], 4); rec["t"] = round(fit.tvalues[term], 2); rec["p slope"] = fit.pvalues[term]
    for g in ("NH", "EN"):
        dg = d[d.group == g]
        ts = stats.theilslopes(dg.weak, dg.strong)
        rec[f"Theil-Sen slope {g} (95% CI)"] = f"{ts[0]:.4f} ({ts[2]:.4f}, {ts[3]:.4f})"
        rec[f"Huber slope {g}"] = round(sm.RLM(dg.weak, sm.add_constant(dg.strong), M=sm.robust.norms.HuberT()).fit().params["strong"], 4)
        q = dg.strong.quantile(0.99)
        rec[f"OLS slope {g}, strongest-four below 99th pct"] = round(smf.ols("weak ~ strong", data=dg[dg.strong <= q]).fit().params["strong"], 4)
    rows.append(rec)
    if resp == "methods":
        DABS = d

Somatotopic receptive fields (Figure 4D and 4E)¶

For ROIs over a barrel, the response to the CW and to its neighbours: -1 row is the whisker one row dorsal in the same arc (C2 for D2), +1 row one row ventral (E2), -1 arc one arc caudal in the same row (D1), +1 arc one arc rostral (D3), for ROIs whose CW has that neighbour among the nine. "Columns with at least 3 ROIs" is applied per field and barrel; all columns is the other reading.

In [35]:
def neighbour(cw, dr, da):
    r, a = "cde".index(cw[0]) + dr, int(cw[1]) + da
    return f"{'cde'[r]}{a}" if 0 <= r < 3 and 1 <= a <= 3 else None


def somato(tb, ar, layer, sel=None, zkey="z", min_col=None):
    m = (tb.layer == layer).values & tb.inb.values
    if sel is not None:
        m = m & sel
    if min_col:
        cnt = tb[m].groupby(["field", "barrel"]).size()
        okc = set(cnt[cnt >= min_col].index)
        m = m & np.array([(f, b) in okc for f, b in zip(tb.field, tb.barrel)])
    out = {}
    for g in ("NH", "EN"):
        idx = np.where(m & (tb.group == g).values)[0]
        rec = {"CW": [], "-1 row": [], "+1 row": [], "-1 arc": [], "+1 arc": []}
        for i in idx:
            cw = tb.barrel.iat[i]
            rec["CW"].append(ar[zkey][i, ssc10.WHISKERS.index(cw)])
            for name, dr, da in (("-1 row", -1, 0), ("+1 row", 1, 0), ("-1 arc", 0, -1), ("+1 arc", 0, 1)):
                nb = neighbour(cw, dr, da)
                if nb is not None:
                    rec[name].append(ar[zkey][i, ssc10.WHISKERS.index(nb)])
        out[g] = {k: np.array(v, float) for k, v in rec.items()}
    return out


def somato_table(o, rng):
    rows = []
    for k in ("CW", "-1 row", "+1 row", "-1 arc", "+1 arc"):
        a, b = o["EN"][k], o["NH"][k]
        d, p = ssc10.perm_test_means(a, b, rng)
        rows.append(dict(whisker=k, n_NH=int(np.isfinite(b).sum()), NH=np.nanmean(b), sem_NH=ssc10.sem(b),
                         n_EN=int(np.isfinite(a).sum()), EN=np.nanmean(a), sem_EN=ssc10.sem(a), diff=d, p=p))
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).set_index("whisker")


SOM = {}

    for mc in (3, None):
        for zkey in ("z", "zmed"):
            SOM[("L23", resp, mc, zkey)] = somato_table(somato(tb, ar, "L23", None, zkey, mc), rng)
            SOM[("L4", resp, mc, zkey)] = somato_table(somato(tb, ar, "L4", tb.c123.values, zkey, mc), rng)

In L2/3, EN reduced responses to the surround whiskers one row dorsal and one row ventral to the CW (from 68% and 62% of the CW response in NH to 49% and 41% in EN), sharpening receptive fields across rows.

    for k, (nh, tnh, en, ten, fn, fe) in {"-1 row": (0.44, 0.02, 0.35, 0.02, 68, 49), "+1 row": (0.39, 0.02, 0.29, 0.01, 62, 41)}.items():
        rec[f"{k} NH/EN"] = f"{s.loc[k, 'NH']:.3f}/{s.loc[k, 'EN']:.3f}"; rec[f"{k} p"] = s.loc[k, "p"]
        pn, pe = 100 * s.loc[k, "NH"] / s.loc["CW", "NH"], 100 * s.loc[k, "EN"] / s.loc["CW", "EN"]

        within += int(abs(s.loc[k, "NH"] - nh) <= tnh) + int(abs(s.loc[k, "EN"] - en) <= ten)

fig5a-l23-signal-correlation-boundary¶

In L2/3, EN modestly raised signal correlation for within-column pairs (0.637 to 0.659) and greatly reduced it for across-column pairs (0.541 to 0.425); in EN, closely spaced pairs (under 150 um) had much lower signal correlation across than within columns (0.529 against 0.674), where in NH the difference was modest (0.611 against 0.652).

In [41]:
def corr_summary(pp, layer, key, rng):
    p = pp[pp.layer == layer]
    out = {}
    for g in ("NH", "EN"):
        for same in (True, False):
            s = p[(p.group == g) & (p.same == same)][key]
            out[(g, same, "all")] = s
            out[(g, same, "<150")] = p[(p.group == g) & (p.same == same) & (p.dist < 150)][key]
    res = {}
    for k, s in out.items():
        res[k] = (s.mean(), ssc10.sem(s), len(s))
    tests = {
        "within EN vs NH": ssc10.perm_test_means(out[("EN", True, "all")], out[("NH", True, "all")], rng),
        "across EN vs NH": ssc10.perm_test_means(out[("EN", False, "all")], out[("NH", False, "all")], rng),
        "NH <150 within vs across": ssc10.perm_test_means(out[("NH", True, "<150")], out[("NH", False, "<150")], rng),
        "EN <150 within vs across": ssc10.perm_test_means(out[("EN", True, "<150")], out[("EN", False, "<150")], rng),
    }
    return res, tests

    for k, (d, p) in tests.items():

fig5b-l23-noise-correlation-boundary¶

In L2/3 of NH mice, noise correlations were similar within (0.334) and across (0.327) columns; EN modestly reduced them within columns (0.307) and greatly reduced them across columns (0.255), even for pairs about 100 um apart.

In [43]:
rng = np.random.default_rng(602)
EXP5B = {("NH", True): (0.334, 0.002), ("NH", False): (0.327, 0.002), ("EN", True): (0.307, 0.001), ("EN", False): (0.255, 0.001)}
for resp, pp in PAIRS.items():
    p = pp[pp.layer == "L23"]
    print(f"Responsiveness: {resp}")
    for (g, same), (e, tol) in EXP5B.items():
        s = p[(p.group == g) & (p.same == same)].noise
        print(f"  {g} {'within' if same else 'across'}: {s.mean():.4f} +/- {ssc10.sem(s):.4f} (n = {len(s)}); paper {e} +/- {tol}; within: {abs(s.mean() - e) <= tol}")
    w = ssc10.perm_test_means(p[(p.group == "EN") & p.same].noise, p[(p.group == "NH") & p.same].noise, rng)
    a = ssc10.perm_test_means(p[(p.group == "EN") & ~p.same].noise, p[(p.group == "NH") & ~p.same].noise, rng)
    near = p[~p.same & (p.dist >= 75) & (p.dist < 125)]
    n = ssc10.perm_test_means(near[near.group == "EN"].noise, near[near.group == "NH"].noise, rng)
    nhw = ssc10.perm_test_means(p[(p.group == "NH") & p.same].noise, p[(p.group == "NH") & ~p.same].noise, rng)
    print(f"  within EN - NH {w[0]:+.4f} (p = {w[1]:.4g}); across EN - NH {a[0]:+.4f} (p = {a[1]:.4g}); across reduction larger: {a[0] < w[0]}")
    print(f"  across-column pairs 75-125 um apart: NH {near[near.group == 'NH'].noise.mean():.4f} (n = {(near.group == 'NH').sum()}),"
          f" EN {near[near.group == 'EN'].noise.mean():.4f} (n = {(near.group == 'EN').sum()}), p = {n[1]:.4g}")

fig5eh-l23-correlation-gradient-at-edge¶

EN substantially reduced the signal and noise correlations of neurons outside a reference column to neurons inside it, while preserving signal correlation and modestly reducing noise correlation within the column, giving a steeper gradient at the column edge.

For each responsive L2/3 ROI over a barrel and each reference column of its field holding other such ROIs, the mean correlation to the ROIs in that column; inside when the ROI is in the column.

In [44]:
def to_column(pp, layer="L23"):
    p = pp[pp.layer == layer]
    both = pd.concat([p.rename(columns={"i": "a", "j": "b", "bi": "ba", "bj": "bb"}),
                      p.rename(columns={"j": "a", "i": "b", "bj": "ba", "bi": "bb"})])
    g = both.groupby(["group", "field", "a", "ba", "bb"])[["signal", "noise"]].mean().reset_index()
    g["inside"] = g.ba == g.bb
    return g


rng = np.random.default_rng(603)
for resp, pp in PAIRS.items():
    g = to_column(pp)
    print(f"Responsiveness: {resp}; ROI-column entries inside {int(g.inside.sum())}, outside {int((~g.inside).sum())}")
    for key in ("signal", "noise"):
        ins = ssc10.perm_test_means(g[(g.group == "EN") & g.inside][key], g[(g.group == "NH") & g.inside][key], rng)
        out = ssc10.perm_test_means(g[(g.group == "EN") & ~g.inside][key], g[(g.group == "NH") & ~g.inside][key], rng)
        print(f"  {key}: inside NH {g[(g.group == 'NH') & g.inside][key].mean():.4f} EN {g[(g.group == 'EN') & g.inside][key].mean():.4f}"
              f" (EN - NH {ins[0]:+.4f}, p = {ins[1]:.4g}); outside NH {g[(g.group == 'NH') & ~g.inside][key].mean():.4f}"
              f" EN {g[(g.group == 'EN') & ~g.inside][key].mean():.4f} (EN - NH {out[0]:+.4f}, p = {out[1]:.4g});"
              f" more negative outside: {out[0] < ins[0]}")
        # Test of the gradient: (EN - NH outside) - (EN - NH inside), group labels shuffled within
        # inside and within outside entries (10,000 shuffles, two-sided). Not in the paper or the
        # criterion; added to show whether the outside-inside difference is distinguishable from zero.
        gk = g[np.isfinite(g[key])]
        x_in, x_out = gk[gk.inside][key].values, gk[~gk.inside][key].values
        en_in, en_out = (gk[gk.inside].group == "EN").values, (gk[~gk.inside].group == "EN").values
        obs = (x_out[en_out].mean() - x_out[~en_out].mean()) - (x_in[en_in].mean() - x_in[~en_in].mean())
        cnt = 0
        for _ in range(10):
            Mi = ssc10.perm_masks(int(en_in.sum()), int((~en_in).sum()), rng, 1000).astype(float)
            Mo = ssc10.perm_masks(int(en_out.sum()), int((~en_out).sum()), rng, 1000).astype(float)
            xi = np.concatenate([x_in[en_in], x_in[~en_in]]); xo = np.concatenate([x_out[en_out], x_out[~en_out]])
            di = Mi @ xi / en_in.sum() - (1 - Mi) @ xi / (~en_in).sum()
            do = Mo @ xo / en_out.sum() - (1 - Mo) @ xo / (~en_out).sum()
            cnt += (np.abs(do - di) >= abs(obs) - 1e-12).sum()
        print(f"    {key}: (EN - NH outside) - (EN - NH inside) = {obs:+.4f}, permutation p = {(cnt + 1) / 10001:.4g}")
    print()

Result: reproduced (changed from partially reproduced after round 3 of the verification). EN lowers the correlations of ROIs outside a column to that column (Methods' test: signal -0.091, noise -0.045, both p = 0.0001; stored p-values -0.043, p = 0.0016, and -0.043, p = 0.0001), and inside the column the signal correlation is not lower (p = 0.39 and 0.19). The EN minus NH difference is more negative outside than inside for signal and for noise (-0.0454 against -0.0450 with the Methods' test, -0.0430 against -0.0409 with the stored p-values), so every condition of the criterion holds in both readings. The signal gradient is steeper in EN by a test as well: the outside minus inside difference of EN minus NH is -0.080 (p = 0.0002) and -0.061 (p = 0.0013). The noise gradient is not: the noise reduction is about the same outside and inside (difference -0.0004, p = 0.96; stored -0.0020, p = 0.81). The permutation test is not part of the criterion, but the noise half passes on differences that cannot be told from zero, and in the first run the Methods' reading failed by 0.0002 (-0.0459 against -0.0461). The paper contrasts a substantial reduction outside with a modest one inside; the criterion reduces this to a sign comparison without a test or margin, which is raised as a question on the claims file.

figs5-2-neuropil-robustness¶

The enrichment effects on tuning heterogeneity and point representation were qualitatively unchanged with neuropil subtraction at r = 0, 0.3 and 0.7 in L2/3 and L4; effects on signal correlations held at r = 0 and 0.3 but were lost at 0.7, and effects on noise correlations held at all levels.

dF/F is rebuilt from rawTimeSeries and rawTimeSeriesNP_corr at each weight (helper, _dff), and the whole pipeline is re-run: responsiveness by the Methods' test, eBWs (E1, E2), the z-scored responses, and the pair correlations. The correlation test is the one the Figure 5 S2 legend names, an ANOVA with multiple comparisons, read as a one-way ANOVA over NH and EN within and across columns with Tukey comparisons; the permutation test is the variant.

Result: not reproduced. At r = 0, 0.3 and 0.7 the L2/3 fraction CW-tuned at 0-75 um is lower in EN under E1 and E2 (for example 92%, 93%, 81% in NH against 83%, 80%, 74% in EN, E1), as without subtraction. The other three directions hold at every weight: the L2/3 0-75 um response is higher in EN, the L4 fraction CW-tuned is higher and the L4 0-75 um response lower. The criterion asks only for the direction; none of the response differences is significant (L2/3 p = 0.30, 0.57, 0.93; L4 p = 0.80, 0.44, 0.73). At r = 0 the rebuild gives 815 EN and 460 NH responsive L2/3 ROIs, against 850 and 472 from the stored traces in the main analysis, because the 89 L2/3 ROIs with non-finite rebuilt traces are given p = 1 and so count as unresponsive at every weight. The across-column signal correlation reduction is significant at r = 0 and 0.3 (Tukey p < 0.001) and not at 0.7 (p = 0.084), as the paper finds. The across-column noise correlation reduction is significant at every weight, but the within-column one is not at r = 0.7 (Tukey p = 0.996). So two parts of the criterion fail: the L2/3 tuning direction, which follows from the eBW fractions (figs3-1-l23-salt-and-pepper), and the within-column noise reduction at r = 0.7.

Decoding (Figure 7)¶

Each ROI's classifier is a logistic regression of stimulus (one whisker) against blank on the single-trial evoked response, fit on the training trials of a split and applied to the test trials; the predicted class is the more probable one (Methods, Neural decoder). L2/3 responsive ROIs.

In [49]:
def nearest_col(f, r):
    d = np.linalg.norm(f["pos"][r], axis=-1)
    d = np.where([f["ev"][w].shape[1] > 0 for w in ssc10.WHISKERS], d, np.inf)
    return int(np.nanargmin(d))

                    targets["CW"] = ssc10.WHISKERS.index(f["barrel"][r])
                for name, j in targets.items():
                    w = ssc10.WHISKERS[j]
                    x = np.concatenate([f["ev"][w][r], f["bl"][r]])
                    y = np.concatenate([np.ones(f["ev"][w].shape[1]), np.zeros(f["bl"].shape[1])])
                    if j not in splits:
                        splits[j] = ssc10.make_splits(f["ev"][w].shape[1], f["bl"].shape[1], rng, scheme, 500, balance)
                    tr, te = splits[j]
                    _, acc = ssc10.roi_probs(x, y, tr, te)
                    rows.append(dict(field=f["field"], mouse=f["mouse"], group=f["group"], roi=r, target=name, scheme=scheme,
                                     balance=balance, acc=acc.mean(), chance=max(y.mean(), 1 - y.mean()) if not balance else 0.5))
DEC1 = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"single-ROI decoders: {len(DEC1)} fits of 400-500 splits each, {time.time() - t0:.0f} s")

fig7c-population-decoder¶

Detection by population decoders of randomly chosen, simultaneously imaged ROIs improved with ensemble size and was better for EN than NH for ensembles of 3 or more neurons.

Ensembles of 1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25 and 30 responsive ROIs of a field, the lesser of 500 and N-choose-K per field and size (Methods). Classifiers are fit on 50 random 80/20 splits per field and whisker, shared by all ROIs of the field (the Methods give no number of repetitions for ensembles; 50 is a standard choice made for time). The ensemble sums each class's probability over its ROIs (normalisation (a)), or sums each ROI's probability z-scored over the test trials (b).

In [51]:
N_SPLIT_ENS = 50
SIZES = [1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30]


def field_probs(f, rows_r, rng, n_split=N_SPLIT_ENS):
    """For each whisker: (P: splits x ROIs x trials, y, test masks)."""
    out = {}
    for j, w in enumerate(ssc10.WHISKERS):
        ns = f["ev"][w].shape[1]
        if ns == 0:
            continue
        nb = f["bl"].shape[1]
        tr, te = ssc10.make_splits(ns, nb, rng, "random", n_split, False)
        y = np.concatenate([np.ones(ns), np.zeros(nb)])
        P = np.stack([ssc10.roi_probs(np.concatenate([f["ev"][w][r], f["bl"][r]]), y, tr, te)[0] for r in rows_r], axis=1)
        # normalisation (b): each ROI's probability z-scored over the test trials of the split
        Pm = np.where(te[:, None, :], P, np.nan)
        Z = (P - np.nanmean(Pm, 2, keepdims=True)) / (np.nanstd(Pm, 2, keepdims=True) + 1e-12)
        out[j] = (P, Z, y, te)
    return out


def ens_acc(P, Z, y, te, members, norm):
    if norm == "a":
        s = P[:, members, :].sum(1)
        score = s - (len(members) - s)                          # summed P(stim) minus summed P(blank)
    else:
        score = Z[:, members, :].sum(1)
    pred = score > 0
    return (((pred == (y > 0.5)) & te).sum(1) / te.sum(1)).mean()


rng = np.random.default_rng(803)
rows = []
t0 = time.time()
PROBS = {}
for fi, f in enumerate(F):
    if f["layer"] != "L23":
        continue
    rows_r = np.where(f["resp_methods"])[0]
    N = len(rows_r)
    probs = field_probs(f, rows_r, rng)
    PROBS[fi] = (rows_r, probs)
    col = np.array([ssc10.WHISKERS.index(f["barrel"][r]) if f["barrel"][r] else nearest_col(f, r) for r in rows_r])
    for K in SIZES:
        if K > N:
            continue
        n_ens = min(500, comb(N, K))
        seen = set()
        while len(seen) < n_ens:
            seen.add(tuple(sorted(rng.choice(N, K, replace=False))))
        for ens in seen:
            ens = np.array(ens)
            cen = f["pos"][rows_r[ens]].mean(0)                  # 9 x 2, centroid relative to each barrel
            dcen = np.linalg.norm(cen, axis=-1)
            dcen = np.where([j in probs for j in range(9)], dcen, np.inf)
            j_close = int(np.argmin(dcen))
            rec = dict(fi=fi, field=f["field"], group=f["group"], K=K)
            for norm in ("a", "b"):
                rec[f"close_{norm}"] = ens_acc(*probs[j_close], ens, norm)
                cws = sorted(set(col[ens]) & set(probs))
                rec[f"cws_{norm}"] = np.mean([ens_acc(*probs[j], ens, norm) for j in cws])
            rows.append(rec)
ENS = pd.DataFrame(rows)
print(f"random ensembles: {len(ENS)} in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s; per field and size:")
print(ENS.groupby(["group", "K"]).size().unstack().to_string())

Result: reproduced, under one reading. With ensembles pooled as units, performance rises with ensemble size in both groups (closest-column whisker, normalisation a: NH 0.611 to 0.674, EN 0.627 to 0.710 from 1 to 30 ROIs) and EN exceeds NH with p < 0.001 at every size from 3 on, under all four combinations of tested whisker and normalisation. With the CWs of the members and normalisation (a) performance does not rise steadily (NH 0.628 at 3 ROIs and 0.627 at 5; EN 0.674 at 10 to 15 ROIs and 0.671 at 30); so the rise holds under the other three combinations, and the outcome needs only one. With per-field means as units no size reaches p < 0.001 (p from 0.024 to 0.42 over 11 fields per group). The pooled ensembles reuse the same ROIs many times within a field, so the pooled p-values overstate the evidence; the criterion allows the pooled unit.

fig7d-clustered-ensemble-topography¶

Spatially clustered ensembles detected the reference whisker best near its column centre; EN decoders outperformed NH decoders for ensembles centred 0-77 and 77-154 um from the column centre, and EN performed worse than NH farther away (e.g. 308-385 um).

For each field and reference whisker, k-means on the responsive ROIs' positions normalised to the reference barrel (ROI_pos_barrel_norm), for every k from 2 to the number of responsive ROIs (Methods); clusters of 2 to 42 ROIs are ensembles. k-means is scipy.cluster.vq.kmeans2 with k-means++ starts, one run per k (a standard choice). Each ensemble detects its reference whisker against blank (normalisation (a), the 50 splits above); its centroid's distance to the reference column centre is in um (ROI_pos_barrel), in 77 um bins.

In [53]:
from scipy.cluster.vq import kmeans2

rng = np.random.default_rng(805)
rows = []
t0 = time.time()
for fi, (rows_r, probs) in PROBS.items():
    f = F[fi]
    N = len(rows_r)
    for j in probs:
        X = f["posn"][rows_r, j]
        ok = np.isfinite(X).all(1)
        for k in range(2, N + 1):
            _, lab = kmeans2(X[ok], k, minit="++", seed=rng)
            for c in range(k):
                ens = np.where(ok)[0][lab == c]
                if not 2 <= len(ens) <= 42:
                    continue
                d = np.linalg.norm(f["pos"][rows_r[ens], j].mean(0))
                rows.append(dict(fi=fi, field=f["field"], group=f["group"], ref=j, k=k, K=len(ens), dist=d,
                                 acc=ens_acc(*probs[j], ens, "a")))
CLU = pd.DataFrame(rows)
CLU["bin"] = (CLU.dist // 77).astype(int)
print(f"clustered ensembles: {len(CLU)} in {time.time() - t0:.0f} s; per field: ",
      CLU.groupby(["group", "field"]).size().groupby("group").agg(["mean", "std"]).round(0).to_dict("index"))

How the analysis differs from the paper's. The responsiveness test is the Methods' one-sided test of means; the p-values stored in the data set come from a two-sided test on medians (permTestType 'median'), and the two agree on 86% of ROIs. Both are shown, and three outcomes (fig2a, fig4b, fig4d-cw) rest on the stored ones. The equivalent best whiskers are computed by three readings the claims file names, since neither the Methods nor the code say how; all three put many more L2/3 NH cells near a column centre in the tuned group than the paper reports, while the NH L4 values match under E1 and E2 (under E3 the L4 eBW value is 82.1%, outside tolerance). An exploratory reading outside the claims file, which also requires each equivalent whisker to be responsive, comes near the paper's NH values but does not make EN L2/3 more CW-tuned. Barrel radii come from the normalised ROI positions, not from barrel areas. Ensemble decoders use 50 splits per field and whisker, and one k-means run per k.

What was found about the data set. The counts of mice and fields match Table 1, and the NH L2/3 cell count is exact; the EN L2/3 and the L4 totals differ from the paper's (1147 against 1257, 362 against 322, 615 against 586), and processed_data.mat holds more ROIs than reduced_data.mat with no stated rule. One NH field has no E-row whisker trials. The stored dF/F follows the pipeline's 5-frame filter and 5th-percentile F0, not the Methods' 4 frames and 20th percentile. The L4 dF/F subtracts the neuropil after the filter, as the descriptor says. In three L4 fields sponTrace is cut 0.5 s after the blank onsets, unlike every other field. The label code of Stimuli and the blank-trial selection of sponTrace are not documented. No barrel areas are stored, and the cell-attached recordings of Figure 1F are not in the data set.
